You know the ones, the pavement-blocking LED monoliths, with screens on both sides broadcasting six ads per minute to passersby. The ads shown are invariably for global mega-corporations, further driving commerce online, and for unhealthy products such as junk food, alcohol, gambling and vapes (although the latter are to be banned from 1 June 2027). description: I welcome Alan Milburn’s call for schools to focus more on students’ potential beyond exams. Yet I must ask: where is the money? At 16, life should feel like a path leading to endless opportunities. That is at least the carrot dangled in front of young people to motivate them through the gruelling years of exam preparation. “Your life starts now,” their teachers all but tell them. And though for the vast majority that is true, there is a cohort who are forced to accept that the bright futures they were promised are beyond their reach. author: Lucia Cheng and Thao Nguyen, USA TODAY NETWORK

description: Residents in parts of southeastern Iowa and northwest Illinois are being warned about possible lead dust exposure as the U.S. Army prepares to detonate 68 barrels of lead azide that have been stored for more than 20 years at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The barrels cannot be safely transported because the lead azide had become drier and more volatile than expected, according to Justine Barati, deputy chief of public and congressional affairs for Army Sustainment Command. The aging explosive can detonate from movement, friction or other disturbances, and Army officials determined that an on-site detonation was the safest disposal option. The detonation, scheduled for Nov. 20, is expected to generate two rapid explosions and ground vibrations that could potentially damage windows, according to an Army public advisory .
